title: Probability at a binary choice
statement: Let $A$ be a nondeterministic register program with state set $\Lambda$, oracle, input $x$, and $m$ registers. Suppose state $l$ makes a binary choice, proceeding to $l_1$ on choice bit $1$ and to $l_0$ on choice bit $0$. For any register valuation $v$, result value $res$, natural number $N$, and decidable predicate $R$ on configurations, the fraction of length-$(N+1)$ choice strings for which running from state $l$ with valuation $v$ and result $res$ yields a configuration satisfying $R$ equals the average of the corresponding fractions of length-$N$ choice strings starting from $l_1$ and $l_0$.
hypotheses_covered: The program $A$, oracle, input $x$, and register count $m$ are fixed
The instruction at $l$ is the stated binary choice
$R$ is a decidable predicate on configurations
